--- title: "Logistic regression with a categorical predictor" format: html: df-print: kable toc: true toc-depth: 3 number-sections: true --- # Introduction A treatment variable with three arms is a **categorical predictor**, not a single binary treatment indicator. In the STePS data, the arms are waitlist, therapist-guided treatment, and self-guided treatment. Our primary questions are: 1. What is the model-derived probability of treatment response in each treatment arm? 2. How do those probabilities differ between clinically relevant pairs of arms? As before, we will communicate probabilities and probability differences with 95% CIs. Log-odds coefficients and odds ratios help us read model output, but they are not probability differences. # Packages and data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(here) library(broom) library(marginaleffects) options( marginaleffects_print_omit = c("s.value"), marginaleffects_print_style = ifelse(interactive(), "summary", "tinytable") ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df_categorical <- read_csv2(here("data", "steps_clean.csv")) |> filter(!is.na(lsas_screen), !is.na(lsas_post)) |> mutate( # The second level is the event modelled by binomial glm(). lsas_response = factor( if_else((lsas_screen - lsas_post) / lsas_screen >= 0.30, "Response", "No response"), levels = c("No response", "Response") ), trt = factor( trt, levels = c("waitlist", "therapist-guided", "self-guided") ) ) df_categorical |> count(trt, lsas_response, .drop = FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|trt |lsas_response | n| |:----------------|:-------------|--:| |waitlist |No response | 52| |waitlist |Response | 6| |therapist-guided |No response | 23| |therapist-guided |Response | 31| |self-guided |No response | 37| |self-guided |Response | 20|
::: ::: `Response` is a reduction of at least 30% from baseline LSAS; it is not a diagnostic or remission definition. We order the outcome so that `Low` is the event in the binomial model, and we explicitly set `waitlist` as the treatment reference category. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} levels(df_categorical$trt) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "waitlist" "therapist-guided" "self-guided" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} contrasts(df_categorical$trt) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` therapist-guided self-guided waitlist 0 0 therapist-guided 1 0 self-guided 0 1 ``` ::: ::: # Reference categories and dummy variables With waitlist as the reference, R uses two indicator variables. The model is $$ \operatorname{logit}\left[P(Y_i = \text{Response} \mid trt_i)\right] = \beta_0 + \beta_1\,\mathbf{1}\{trt_i = \text{therapist-guided}\} + \beta_2\,\mathbf{1}\{trt_i = \text{self-guided}\}. $$ | Treatment group | Linear predictor | Coefficient comparison | |---|---:|---| | waitlist | $\beta_0$ | reference | | therapist-guided | $\beta_0 + \beta_1$ | therapist-guided minus waitlist | | self-guided | $\beta_0 + \beta_2$ | self-guided minus waitlist | Thus, the coefficient table supplies two log-odds comparisons with waitlist. It does **not** directly show the self-guided-versus-therapist-guided comparison; we obtain that, and all other pairwise probability differences, from the fitted model. # Fit the three-arm logistic model ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mod_categorical_trt <- stats::glm( lsas_response ~ trt, family = binomial, data = df_categorical ) p_categorical_trt <- avg_predictions( mod_categorical_trt, by = "trt", type = "response" ) diff_guided_waitlist <- avg_comparisons( mod_categorical_trt, variables = list(trt = c("waitlist", "therapist-guided")), type = "response" ) diff_self_waitlist <- avg_comparisons( mod_categorical_trt, variables = list(trt = c("waitlist", "self-guided")), type = "response" ) or_categorical_trt <- tidy( mod_categorical_trt, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE ) |> filter(term != "(Intercept)") ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Model interpretation The estimated probability of treatment response is **10.3%** for waitlist (95% CI **2.5%** to **18.2%**), **57.4%** for therapist-guided treatment (95% CI **44.2%** to **70.6%**), and **35.1%** for self-guided treatment (95% CI **22.7%** to **47.5%**). Relative to waitlist, therapist-guided treatment **increases** the estimated probability by **47.1 percentage points** (95% CI **31.7** to **62.4 percentage points**). Self-guided treatment **increases** it by **24.7 percentage points** relative to waitlist (95% CI **10.1** to **39.4 percentage points**). These are unadjusted contrasts in the three-arm analysis sample. The corresponding odds ratios versus waitlist are **11.68** for therapist-guided treatment (95% CI **4.54** to **34.62**) and **4.68** for self-guided treatment (95% CI **1.80** to **13.85**). Each is a ratio of odds, not a probability ratio or a percentage-point probability difference. ::: # Predicted probabilities by treatment arm ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p_categorical_trt ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
trt Estimate Std. Error z Pr(>|z|) 2.5 % 97.5 %
Type: response
waitlist 0.103 0.0400 2.59 0.00968 0.0251 0.182
therapist-guided 0.574 0.0673 8.53 < 0.001 0.4422 0.706
self-guided 0.351 0.0632 5.55 < 0.001 0.2270 0.475
``` ::: ::: The three predicted probabilities are response-scale summaries of the same logistic model. They are often a more direct starting point for a clinical discussion than its intercept and two log-odds coefficients. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_predictions(mod_categorical_trt, by = "trt", type = "response") + labs( title = "Estimated probability of treatment response", subtitle = "Three-arm logistic regression; 95% confidence intervals", x = "Treatment group", y = "Probability of treatment response" ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](logistic-one-categorical-predictor_files/figure-html/plot-categorical-treatment-probabilities-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: # Probability differences between treatment arms There is no single treatment contrast with three arms. Decide which comparison answers the substantive question, state its direction, and present uncertainty. For an exploratory overview, calculate all pairwise differences. A positive difference means that the first-named group has the higher estimated probability of treatment response. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairwise_categorical_differences <- avg_comparisons( mod_categorical_trt, variables = list(trt = "pairwise"), type = "response" ) pairwise_categorical_differences ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
Contrast Estimate Std. Error z Pr(>|z|) 2.5 % 97.5 %
Type: response
self-guided - therapist-guided -0.223 0.0923 -2.42 0.0156 -0.404 -0.0422
self-guided - waitlist 0.247 0.0748 3.31 <0.001 0.101 0.3940
therapist-guided - waitlist 0.471 0.0783 6.01 <0.001 0.317 0.6240
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairwise_categorical_differences |> mutate( estimate_pp = 100 * estimate, conf.low_pp = 100 * conf.low, conf.high_pp = 100 * conf.high ) |> ggplot(aes(y = contrast, x = estimate_pp)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") + geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf.low_pp, xmax = conf.high_pp), width = 0.1) + geom_point(size = 2.5) + labs( title = "Pairwise differences in probability of treatment response", subtitle = "First-named treatment minus second-named treatment; 95% confidence intervals", x = "Probability difference (percentage points)", y = NULL ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](logistic-one-categorical-predictor_files/figure-html/plot-pairwise-categorical-probability-differences-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: # Odds ratios as a secondary summary ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} or_categorical_trt ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|term | estimate| std.error| statistic| p.value| conf.low| conf.high| |:-------------------|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|--------:|---------:| |trttherapist-guided | 11.681159| 0.5114807| 4.805611| 0.0000015| 4.542373| 34.62210| |trtself-guided | 4.684685| 0.5127409| 3.011850| 0.0025966| 1.801915| 13.85084|
::: ::: The odds ratios above compare each active arm with waitlist because waitlist is the reference group. To obtain a self-guided-versus-therapist-guided odds ratio, one could change the reference category or form the appropriate model contrast. Neither route changes the main communication task: accompany any odds ratio with response-scale probabilities and a clearly directed probability difference. # Summary In this chapter you learned to: - define an explicit reference category for a three-level treatment predictor; - fit a three-arm binary logistic model with `stats::glm(..., family = binomial)`; - obtain estimated probabilities for every treatment arm and pairwise probability differences with 95% CIs; and - distinguish odds ratios from the percentage-point probability differences needed for a clinical interpretation.
